extracted.intended_audience: reviewers for the Journal of Machine Learning Research (JMLR)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for performing peer reviews of submissions to the Journal of Machine Learning Research, listing the points reviewers should address about goals, description, evaluation, significance, related work, clarity, and recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goals
rubrics_metrics.description: What are research goals and learning task?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should identify the research goals and the learning task being addressed; touch upon this point as part of the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description (reproducibility and exposition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the description adequately detailed for others to replicate the work? Is it clearly written in good style and does it include examples?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For systems papers: clearly describe the contributions or the principles underlying the system. For theoretical papers: also discuss their practical utility. Assess whether description/detail is sufficient for replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the authors evaluate their work in an adequate way (theoretically and/or empirically)? Are all claims clearly articulated and supported either by empirical experiments or theoretical analyses?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appropriate, check whether the authors have implemented their work and demonstrated its utility on a significant problem. Judge adequacy of experimental design, theoretical argumentation, and whether claims are supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper constitute a significant, technically correct contribution to the field that is appropriate for JMLR? Is it sufficiently different from prior published work (by the author or others) to merit a new publication?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity about how the work advances the current state of understanding and why the advance matters; check for technical correctness and originality relative to prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related Work and Discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Are strength and limitations and generality of the research adequately discussed, in particular in relation to related work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do the authors clearly acknowledge and identify the contributions of their predecessors? Evaluate whether limitations, scope, and generality are addressed and situated with respect to prior literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it written in a way such that an interested reader with a background in machine learning, but no special knowledge of the paper's subject, could understand and appreciate the paper's results?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific points to check: Is it written in a clear, readable style, with good grammar and few (if any) typographical errors? Are the goals and contributions of the work clearly and correctly stated? Are the problem description, approach and evaluation adequately detailed for others to replicate the work? If the paper introduces new terminology or techniques, does it explain why current terminology or techniques are insufficient? Does it include examples?

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation (decision and conditional accept guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please also recommend a decision: accept, conditional accept, reject with encouragement to revise and resubmit, and reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you suggest conditional accept, provide a precise list of changes that can easily be checked upon resubmission. State your recommended decision and, when applicable, exact conditions required for acceptance.
